claims.source: It remains to be determined why TGN/EE localization of VHA-a3-a1-TD is only partial, however it demonstrates that the a1-TD is sufficient to partially re-route VHA-a3 to the TGN/EE.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the localization of VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 represent two clearly separated clades in phylogenetic analysis of VHA-a sequences from mono- and dicot species.
claims.source: Phylogenetic analysis of VHA-a sequences from mono- and dicot species showed that VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 represent two clearly separated clades (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The a1-TD includes a number of amino acids conserved among all of the sequences in the VHA-a1 clade but not in the VHA-a3 clade.
claims.source: The a1-TD includes a number of amino acids conserved among all of the sequences in the VHA-a1 clade (Figure 2A) but not in the VHA-a3 clade that could either be part of a di-acidic ER-export motif or an acidic cluster involved in TGN/EE-retention.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Mutations E161S and F134Y predominantly localized to the TGN/EE.
claims.source: Mutations with high Pearson's correlation coefficients predominately localized to the TGN/EE (E161S and F134Y; Figure 2C,D and K).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Mutations L159T + E161S, L159T, E155 + E156 + I157 deletion (ΔEEI) led to a dual TGN/EE and tonoplast localization.
claims.source: Three mutations led to a dual TGN/EE and tonoplast localization (L159T + E161S, L159T, E155 + E156 + I157 deletion (ΔEEI) and Figure 2E,F,G and H) and had intermediate Pearson's and Mander's coefficients (M2) (Figure 2K).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Mutations E156Q and E156Q + L159T led to VHA-a1 being localized to an unknown compartment.
claims.source: Two mutations led to VHA-a1 being localized to an unknown compartment (E156Q and E156Q + L159T; Figure 2I and J) and had the lowest Pearson's and Mander's coefficients (Figure 2K).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Upon induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP, large clusters of vesicles in the periphery of Golgi stack remnants and ER cisternae appeared swollen.
claims.source: Upon induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP, we observed large clusters of vesicles in the periphery of Golgi stack remnants and ER cisternae appeared swollen (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by electron microscopy images in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP caused ER-retention and colocalization with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP in bright and often large punctae for ST-GFP and BRI1-GFP.
claims.source: Furthermore, in Arabidopsis transgenic lines expressing the Golgi-marker Sialyl transferase (ST; Boevink et al., 1998) or the brassinosteroid receptor (BRI1; Geldner et al., 2007) as GFP fusion proteins, induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP caused their ER-retention and colocalization with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP in bright and often large punctae that might represent the clusters of uncoated COPII vesicles as observed by EM (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The punctate pattern of VHA-a1-GFP disappeared after induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP and was replaced by a characteristic ER pattern with dense punctae that colocalized with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP.
claims.source: Similarly, the punctate pattern of VHA-a1-GFP disappeared after induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP and was replaced by a characteristic ER pattern with dense punctae that colocalized with AtSar1b-GTP-CFP (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: VHA-a3-GFP was not retained in the ER after the induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP.
claims.source: In contrast, VHA-a3-GFP was not retained in the ER after the induction of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: In cells in which VHA-a1-GFP was retained in the ER, VHA-a3-mRFP was not affected.
claims.source: To exclude that these differences in ER retention between VHA-a1-GFP and VHA-a3-GFP were due to differences in induction strength of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP, we also blocked ER exit in a line co-expressing VHA-a1-GFP and VHA-a3-mRFP. In cells in which VHA-a1-GFP was retained in the ER, VHA-a3-mRFP was not affected (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP is partially retained in the ER upon expression of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP.
claims.source: Conversely, VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP is partially retained in the ER upon expression of AtSar1b-GTP-CFP (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: The ER-export of VHA-a1 is COPII-dependent.
claims.source: Taken together, our data confirms that the ER-export of VHA-a1 is COPII-dependent and reveals that the a1-TD contains an ER-export signal.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with dominant negative Sar1 shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: The a1-TD contains an ER-export signal.
claims.source: Taken together, our data confirms that the ER-export of VHA-a1 is COPII-dependent and reveals that the a1-TD contains an ER-export signal.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with dominant negative Sar1 and VHA-a3-a1-TD shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Blocking ER-export causes an increase in the trafficking to the tonoplast via a Golgi-independent route for mutated VHA-a1 proteins.
claims.source: When AtSar1b-GTP was used to block ER exit, we observed a significant increase in the GFP fluorescence intensity at the tonoplast for all the mutated VHA-a1 proteins (Figure 4A and B) indicating that blocking ER-export causes an increase in the trafficking to the tonoplast via a Golgi-independent route.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: When the mutated VHA-a1 proteins were expressed in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant, the ratio of TGN/EE-to-tonoplast fluorescence intensity increased as compared to the wildtype background.
claims.source: Indeed, when the mutated VHA-a1 proteins were expressed in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant, the ratio of TGN/EE-to-tonoplast fluorescence intensity increased as compared to the wildtype background (Figure 5A and B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: VHA-a1 mutants that showed only TGN localization (E161S) or a punctate pattern that is different from VHA-a1-RFP (E156Q and E156Q+ L159T) in the wildtype background displayed a tonoplast signal in the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant.
claims.source: Similarly, VHA-a1 mutants that showed only TGN localization (E161S) or a punctate pattern that is different from VHA-a1-RFP (E156Q and E156Q+ L159T) in the wildtype background displayed a tonoplast signal in the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant (Figure 5A and B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: All mutations affect ER export and the observed tonoplast signal is not a result of poor retention at the TGN/EE but due to a Golgi-independent pathway to the tonoplast.
claims.source: These results strongly support the idea that all mutations affect ER export and that the observed tonoplast signal is not a result of poor retention at the TGN/EE but due to a Golgi-independent pathway to the tonoplast.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the results shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claims.claim: All VHA-a isoforms from seed plants including the gymnosperm Pinus taeda cluster into two distinct clades containing VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 respectively.
claims.source: Our analysis revealed that all VHA-a isoforms from seed plants including the gymnosperm Pinus taeda cluster into two distinct clades containing VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 respectively (Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6A.

claims.claim: The genomes of most basal plants encode multiple isoforms of VHA-a, however they do not fall into either of the VHA-a1 or VHA-a3 clades implying that duplication of VHA-a occurred independently.
claims.source: Interestingly, the genomes of most basal plants encode multiple isoforms of VHA-a, however they do not fall into either of these two clades implying that duplication of VHA-a occurred independently.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The hallmarks of the a1-TD (acidic residues flanking a critical leucine residue) are conserved throughout the angiosperms but are absent in bryophytes, lycophytes, ferns and hornworts.
claims.source: Closer analysis of the a1-TD sequence revealed that the hallmarks of the a1-TD (acidic residues flanking a critical leucine residue) are conserved throughout the angiosperms but are absent in bryophytes, lycophytes, ferns and hornworts.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The gymnosperm sequence from P. taeda contains the a1-TD sequence with the exception of one flanking glutamic residue.
claims.source: Interestingly, the gymnosperm sequence from P. taeda contains the a1-TD sequence with the exception of one flanking glutamic residue (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The Pine and Amborella chimeric proteins colocalized with VHA-a1 at the TGN/EE.
claims.source: Whereas the Pine and Amborella chimeric proteins colocalized with VHA-a1 at the TGN/EE, the Selaginella chimeric protein localized to the tonoplast.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The Selaginella chimeric protein localized to the tonoplast.
claims.source: Whereas the Pine and Amborella chimeric proteins colocalized with VHA-a1 at the TGN/EE, the Selaginella chimeric protein localized to the tonoplast.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The a1-TD domain is conserved within the spermatophytes but not in other green plants.
claims.source: These results suggest that the a1-TD domain is conserved within the spermatophytes but not in other green plants.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the functional complementation experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Complementation of the dwarfed phenotype of the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal.
claims.source: We confirmed that the proteins were expressed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) and observed that complementation of the growth phenotype correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal with VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferring the lowest and VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP the highest degree of rescue (Figure 7A and B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements and localization data shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferred the lowest degree of rescue of the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant.
claims.source: We confirmed that the proteins were expressed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) and observed that complementation of the growth phenotype correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal with VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferring the lowest and VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP the highest degree of rescue (Figure 7A and B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP conferred the highest degree of rescue of the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant.
claims.source: We confirmed that the proteins were expressed (Figure 7—figure supplement 2) and observed that complementation of the growth phenotype correlated with the intensity of the tonoplast signal with VHA-a1E161S-GFP conferring the lowest and VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP the highest degree of rescue (Figure 7A and B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: All VHA-a1-GFP mutation lines had more acidic vacuoles than the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant but none of them reached wildtype vacuolar pH.
claims.source: Whereas all VHA-a1-GFP mutation lines had more acidic vacuoles than the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant none of them reached wildtype vacuolar pH (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by cell sap pH measurements shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: VHA-a1 containing complexes are functional when mistargeted to the tonoplast but their enzymatic properties are different and they cannot fully replace the vacuolar isoforms.
claims.source: Taken together, our data indicates that although VHA-a1 containing complexes are functional when mistargeted to the tonoplast their enzymatic properties are different and they cannot fully replace the vacuolar isoforms.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the complementation and pH measurement data shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus driven by the CaMV35S or MpEF1α promoter predominantly localized to the vacuolar membrane, but some additional punctate structures were detectable.
claims.source: MpVHA-a-mVenus driven by the CaMV35S or MpEF1α promoter predominantly localized to the vacuolar membrane, but some additional punctate structures were detectable (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus localization at the tonoplast of root cells was clearly visible.
claims.source: Next, we expressed a MpVHA-a-mVenus fusion construct (UBQ10:MpVHA-a-mVenus) in the Arabidopsis wildtype background. Whereas MpVHA-a-mVenus localization at the tonoplast of root cells was clearly visible (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), a clear punctate pattern was not observed.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: After BFA treatment, the core of BFA compartments was labeled with MpVHA-a-mVenus indicating that MpVHA-a is also present at the TGN/EE.
claims.source: However, after BFA treatment, the core of BFA compartments was labeled with MpVHA-a-mVenus (Figure 8—figure supplement 2) indicating that MpVHA-a is also present at the TGN/EE.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus localized to the TGN/EE and tonoplast and was found in the core of FM4-64 labeled BFA compartments in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant background.
claims.source: To test for functionality, MpVHA-a-mVenus was expressed in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant background. MpVHA-a-mVenus localized to the TGN/EE and tonoplast and was found in the core of FM4-64 labeled BFA compartments (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by confocal microscopy images in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: V-ATPases that incorporate MpVHA-a can complement the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant to wildtype levels in terms of rosette size and cell sap pH.
claims.source: A growth assay conducted in short day conditions (SD; 22 °C and 10 hr light) revealed that V-ATPases that incorporate MpVHA-a can complement the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant to wildtype levels in terms of rosette size and cell sap pH (Figure 8B and C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area and cell sap pH measurements shown in Figure 8B and C.

claims.claim: Homozygous and bi-allelic vha-a1 individuals were indistinguishable from wildtype during vegetative growth.
claims.source: Surprisingly, we did not only identify heterozygous vha-a1/+ but also homozygous and bi-allelic vha-a1 individuals (Supplementary file 1). The latter two were indistinguishable from wildtype during vegetative growth (Figure 9B), but failed to produce seeds due to a defect in pollen development (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 9B.

claims.claim: vha-a1 mutants failed to produce seeds due to a defect in pollen development.
claims.source: Surprisingly, we did not only identify heterozygous vha-a1/+ but also homozygous and bi-allelic vha-a1 individuals (Supplementary file 1). The latter two were indistinguishable from wildtype during vegetative growth (Figure 9B), but failed to produce seeds due to a defect in pollen development (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Alexander staining of pollen shown in Figure 9C.

claims.claim: vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP under the control of UBQ10 promoter showed normal pollen development.
claims.source: Importantly, all plants with no wildtype allele of either VHA-a1 or VHA-a1-GFP were defective in pollen development, whereas vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP under the control of UBQ10 promoter showed normal pollen development (Figure 9C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Alexander staining of pollen shown in Figure 9C.

claims.claim: Transmission of vha-a1-1 via the male gametophyte required the presence of VHA-a1-GFP.
claims.source: As expected, vha-a1-1 was only transmitted via the male gametophyte in the presence of VHA-a1-GFP.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by genetic crosses shown in Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: Transmission of vha-a1-1 via the female gametophyte did not require the presence of the transgene indicating that development of the female gametophyte is not affected.
claims.source: In contrast, transmission of vha-a1-1 via the female gametophyte did not require the presence of the transgene indicating that development of the female gametophyte is not affected (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by genetic crosses shown in Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: MpVHA-a-mVenus did not rescue the pollen phenotype of vha-a1.
claims.source: Using this strategy, we identified bi–allelic and homozygous vha-a1 mutants expressing UBQ10:MpVHA-a-mVenus and found that it was localized both at the TGN/EE and the tonoplast (Figure 9—figure supplement 2). However, MpVHA-a-mVenus did not rescue the pollen phenotype of vha-a1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2) indicating that the TGN/EE-localized V-ATPase of seed plants has acquired a unique function during pollen development.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Alexander staining of pollen shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The TGN/EE-localized V-ATPase of seed plants has acquired a unique function during pollen development.
claims.source: Using this strategy, we identified bi–allelic and homozygous vha-a1 mutants expressing UBQ10:MpVHA-a-mVenus and found that it was localized both at the TGN/EE and the tonoplast (Figure 9—figure supplement 2). However, MpVHA-a-mVenus did not rescue the pollen phenotype of vha-a1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 2) indicating that the TGN/EE-localized V-ATPase of seed plants has acquired a unique function during pollen development.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the failure of MpVHA-a to rescue the pollen phenotype.

claims.claim: vha-a1 is hypersensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Concanamycin-A (ConcA).
claims.source: However, vha-a1 is hypersensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Concanamycin-A (ConcA).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by hypocotyl length measurements shown in Figure 10A.

claims.claim: vha-a1 vha-a1-GFP etiolated seedlings displayed shorter hypocotyls and had deformed roots in contrast to vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP.
claims.source: Analysis of the progeny of vha-a1 VHA-a1-GFP (Cas9+) mutants revealed that vha-a1 vha-a1-GFP etiolated seedlings displayed shorter hypocotyls and had deformed roots in contrast to vha-a1 mutants expressing VHA-a1-GFP.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by hypocotyl length measurements and root morphology shown in Figure 10A and Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: A target of ConcA is present at the TGN/EE in vha-a1 albeit in small amounts or with a higher sensitivity to ConcA.
claims.source: This result indicates that a target of ConcA is present at the TGN/EE in vha-a1 albeit in small amounts or with a higher sensitivity to ConcA. (Figure 10A and Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the hypersensitivity of vha-a1 to ConcA.

claims.claim: vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ mutants were significantly smaller than vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ individuals indicating that tonoplast V-ATPases compensate for the lack of VHA-a1 during vegetative growth.
claims.source: To test if VHA-a2 or VHA-a3-containing V-ATPases might compensate for the lack of VHA-a1, vha-a1-1 (Cas9+) was crossed with the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant. vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ mutants obtained from this cross were significantly smaller than vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ individuals indicating that tonoplast V-ATPases indeed compensate for the lack of VHA-a1 during vegetative growth (Figure 10B and Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by rosette area measurements shown in Figure 10B and Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: vha-a1 vha-a2/+ and vha-a1 vha-a3/+ plants both had reduced rosette sizes.
claims.source: Subsequently, vha-a1 (Cas9+) was crossed with vha-a2 and vha-a3 single mutants to determine if both are able to compensate for the lack of VHA-a1. vha-a1 vha-a2/+ and vha-a1 vha-a3/+ plants both had reduced rosette sizes, however the latter showed a stronger reduction which is in accordance with VHA-a3 being expressed at higher levels than VHA-a2 (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: vha-a1 vha-a3/+ showed a stronger reduction in rosette size than vha-a1 vha-a2/+ which is in accordance with VHA-a3 being expressed at higher levels than VHA-a2.
claims.source: Subsequently, vha-a1 (Cas9+) was crossed with vha-a2 and vha-a3 single mutants to determine if both are able to compensate for the lack of VHA-a1. vha-a1 vha-a2/+ and vha-a1 vha-a3/+ plants both had reduced rosette sizes, however the latter showed a stronger reduction which is in accordance with VHA-a3 being expressed at higher levels than VHA-a2 (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between expression levels and phenotype severity.

claims.claim: vha-a1/+ vha-a2/+ vha-a3 was smaller than vha-a1/+ vha-a2 vha-a3/+.
claims.source: To analyze mutants with even lower numbers of VHA-a wildtype alleles vha-a1 (Cas9+) vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ was crossed with the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant. Consistent with the results of the single mutant crosses, vha-a1/+ vha-a2/+ vha-a3 was smaller than vha-a1/+ vha-a2 vha-a3/+.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 10C.

claims.claim: vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3/+ was the smallest mutant found.
claims.source: The smallest plants obtained were vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3/+ (Figure 10C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by plant images shown in Figure 10C.

claims.claim: Neither vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3 nor the homozygous triple mutant vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3 were found, suggesting that they are not viable.
claims.source: Neither did we find vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3 nor the homozygous triple mutant vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3, suggesting that they are not viable.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the absence of these genotypes in the progeny.

claims.claim: Differential targeting mediated by subunit a evolved independently in the different eukaryotic lineages.
claims.source: Whereas the targeting information is contained in the N-terminus of the Golgi-localized yeast isoform Stv1p (Finnigan et al., 2012), it was shown to be provided by the C-terminal part for some of the 17 isoforms of Paramecium tetraurelia that localize the V-ATPase to at least seven different compartments (Wassmer et al., 2006). Moreover, the targeting motif identified in Stv1p (Finnigan et al., 2012) is neither conserved in plant nor mammalian subunit a isoforms implying that differential targeting mediated by subunit a evolved independently in the different eukaryotic lineages.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of conservation of targeting motifs across different lineages.

claims.claim: Marchantia might represent the ancestral ground state with a single VHA-isoform predominantly localized at the tonoplast.
claims.source: With the exception of Marchantia and Salvina culculatta, all other plants outside of the spermatophytes possess multiple VHA-a isoforms, however the a1-TD is not conserved in these plants. Evidence for differential targeting of VHA-a isoforms is missing but it seems reasonable to speculate that differential localization arose independently. Based on this, Marchantia might represent the ancestral ground state with a single VHA-isoform predominantly localized at the tonoplast.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on phylogenetic analysis and localization data.

claims.claim: The identity of the VHA-a isoform can influence a number of biochemical properties including assembly, coupling efficiency, protein abundance and reversible dissociation.
claims.source: The identity of the VHA-a isoform does not only determine the subcellular localization, it can influence a number of biochemical properties including assembly, coupling efficiency, protein abundance and reversible dissociation (Leng et al., 1998; Kawasaki-Nishi et al., 2001b, Kawasaki-Nishi et al., 2001a).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD which are mislocalized to the tonoplast have retained their basal proton-pumping activity.
claims.source: The fact that VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD which are mislocalized to the tonoplast can complement the dwarf phenotype of the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant to varying degrees argues strongly that they have retained their basal proton-pumping activity and do not require the specific lipid-environment of the TGN/EE for functionality.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the complementation data shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD do not require the specific lipid-environment of the TGN/EE for functionality.
claims.source: The fact that VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD which are mislocalized to the tonoplast can complement the dwarf phenotype of the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant to varying degrees argues strongly that they have retained their basal proton-pumping activity and do not require the specific lipid-environment of the TGN/EE for functionality.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the complementation data shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: In Arabidopsis, cells that require large quantities of tonoplast membranes such as the cells of the root tip, the VHA-a isoforms compete for entry into COPII vesicles.
claims.source: We propose here that in Arabidopsis, cells that require large quantities of tonoplast membranes such as the cells of the root tip, the VHA-a isoforms compete for entry into COPII vesicles.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: The ratio of VHA-a1 to VHA-a3 is roughly 1:10 based on RNA expression and enzymatic activity.
claims.source: Assembly of all VO-complexes takes place at the ER with the help of dedicated assembly factors and based on RNA expression and enzymatic activity the ratio of VHA-a1 to VHA-a3 is roughly 1:10 (Hanitzsch et al., 2007; Neubert et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Due to the presence of the a1-TD, the affinity of VHA-a1 for Sec24, the cargo receptor for COPII vesicles, is much higher than the affinity of VHA-a3.
claims.source: We assume that due to the presence of the a1-TD, the affinity of VHA-a1 for Sec24, the cargo receptor for COPII vesicles, is much higher than the affinity of VHA-a3.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: Small quantities of VHA-a3 can enter COPII vesicles but the majority is predominantly sorted into the Golgi-independent route.
claims.source: Small quantities of VHA-a3 can enter COPII vesicles but the majority is predominantly sorted into the Golgi-independent route (Figure 11).
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data and illustrated in Figure 11.

claims.claim: In the absence of VHA-a1, VHA-a2/VHA-a3 would be able to enter the COPII-route more efficiently and would thus be able to compensate for the lack of V-ATPases at the TGN/EE.
claims.source: Similarly, in the absence of VHA-a1, VHA-a2/VHA-a3 would be able to enter the COPII-route more efficiently and would thus be able to compensate for the lack of V-ATPases at the TGN/EE providing an explanation for the lack of a vegetative phenotype of the vha-a1 mutant.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: In the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant in which VHA-a1 is the only remaining target, treatment with the V-ATPase inhibitor ConcA causes an additional increase in vacuolar pH although the localization of VHA-a1 is not affected.
claims.source: We have shown previously that despite their seemingly strict spatial separation, the activities of the V-ATPase at the TGN/EE and the tonoplast are coordinated. In the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant in which VHA-a1 is the only remaining target, treatment with the V-ATPase inhibitor ConcA causes an additional increase in vacuolar pH (Kriegel et al., 2015) although the localization of VHA-a1 is not affected.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: In the RNA-mediated knock-down lines, although levels of VHA-a1 are reduced, they are still sufficient to outcompete VHA-a3 for entry into COPII vesicles.
claims.source: Based on our model, we propose that in the RNA-mediated knock-down lines, although levels of VHA-a1 are reduced, they are still sufficient to outcompete VHA-a3 for entry into COPII vesicles.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

results.result: The authors identified a 48 amino acid region (a1-TD) between residues L132 and E179 in VHA-a1 that is necessary and sufficient for TGN/EE localization. This was demonstrated through chimeric protein experiments showing that constructs with ≥179 amino acids of VHA-a1 N-terminus localized to TGN/EE, while shorter constructs localized only to the tonoplast. The a1-TD is structurally distinct from VHA-a3 and accessible in the assembled V-ATPase complex. When inserted into VHA-a3, the a1-TD partially redirects it to the TGN/EE.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C44 provide converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches (chimeric proteins, structural modeling, functional complementation) that consistently identify the a1-TD region. The localization data (C34-C39), BFA treatment confirmation (C38-C39), structural accessibility (C41-C42), and gain-of-function experiment (C43-C44) all support the conclusion. The data are internally consistent and appropriately controlled.

results.result: Site-directed mutagenesis of conserved amino acids within the a1-TD revealed that mutations affect both ER export and TGN/EE retention. Mutations produced three classes of localization patterns: TGN/EE only (E161S, F134Y), dual TGN/EE and tonoplast (L159T+E161S, L159T, ΔEEI), and unknown compartment (E156Q, E156Q+L159T). The authors conclude that all mutations affect ER export rather than TGN/EE retention based on experiments showing increased tonoplast signal when ER export is blocked.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C49 present systematic mutagenesis data with quantitative colocalization analysis (Pearson's and Mander's coefficients). Claim C61 is supported by experiments in Figures 4-5 showing that blocking COPII-mediated export increases tonoplast localization and that mutations have enhanced effects in the vha-a2 vha-a3 background. The interpretation is logical and well-supported by the data.

results.result: The authors demonstrate that VHA-a1 ER export is COPII-dependent and that the a1-TD contains an ER-export signal. Using inducible expression of dominant-negative AtSar1b-GTP to block COPII vesicle formation, they show that VHA-a1-GFP is retained in the ER while VHA-a3-GFP is not. VHA-a3-a1-TD-GFP shows partial ER retention, and blocking ER export increases tonoplast localization of mutated VHA-a1 proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C58 provide strong evidence through multiple complementary experiments: EM showing vesicle accumulation (C50), positive controls with ST-GFP and BRI1-GFP (C51), differential retention of VHA-a1 vs VHA-a3 (C52-C54), and gain-of-function with VHA-a3-a1-TD (C55). The conclusion that a1-TD contains an ER-export signal (C56-C57) is well-supported. Statistical analysis confirms significance (C58).

results.result: Expression of mutated VHA-a1 proteins in the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant background increased the TGN/EE-to-tonoplast fluorescence ratio compared to wildtype background. Mutations that showed only TGN or unknown compartment localization in wildtype displayed tonoplast signal in the double mutant. The authors conclude this demonstrates that mutations affect ER export and tonoplast localization occurs via a Golgi-independent pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C61 present a logical genetic experiment testing whether tonoplast localization results from poor TGN/EE retention or alternative ER exit. The increased TGN/EE ratio in the absence of competing VHA-a2/a3 (C59) and appearance of tonoplast signal for previously TGN-only mutants (C60) support the interpretation that mutations affect ER export (C61). The data are quantified and statistically analyzed.

results.result: Phylogenetic analysis reveals that VHA-a isoforms from seed plants cluster into two distinct clades (VHA-a1 and VHA-a3), while basal plants have multiple isoforms that do not fall into these clades. The a1-TD sequence hallmarks (acidic residues flanking a leucine) are conserved in angiosperms and partially in gymnosperms (P. taeda) but absent in bryophytes, lycophytes, ferns, and hornworts. Functional complementation experiments show that Pine and Amborella chimeric proteins localize to TGN/EE while Selaginella localizes to tonoplast, confirming the a1-TD is functionally conserved within spermatophytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C68 combine phylogenetic analysis (C62-C63) with sequence conservation analysis (C64-C65) and functional validation (C66-C68). The phylogenetic tree is properly constructed with bootstrap support, sequence alignments clearly show conservation patterns, and functional complementation provides direct evidence for conservation. The conclusion that a1-TD is conserved in spermatophytes (C68) is well-supported by converging evidence.

results.result: Mislocalized VHA-a1 mutant proteins can partially complement the vha-a2 vha-a3 double mutant dwarf phenotype, with complementation correlating with tonoplast signal intensity. VHA-a1ΔEEI-GFP provided the highest rescue while VHA-a1E161S-GFP provided the lowest. All mutant lines had more acidic vacuoles than vha-a2 vha-a3 but none reached wildtype pH. The authors conclude that VHA-a1 complexes are functional at the tonoplast but have different enzymatic properties and cannot fully replace vacuolar isoforms.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C73 present complementation data with quantitative measurements of rosette area (C69-C71) and cell sap pH (C72). The correlation between tonoplast localization and complementation is clear, and the failure to fully restore wildtype pH (C72) supports the conclusion about functional differences (C73). Western blots confirm protein expression. The interpretation is appropriately cautious about the mechanistic basis of incomplete complementation.

results.result: The single Marchantia polymorpha VHA-a isoform (MpVHA-a) localizes predominantly to the vacuolar membrane in Marchantia with some punctate structures, and to both tonoplast and TGN/EE in Arabidopsis (confirmed by BFA treatment). When expressed in the Arabidopsis vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant, MpVHA-a-mVenus fully complements the dwarf phenotype and restores cell sap pH to wildtype levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C78 demonstrate dual localization of MpVHA-a through confocal microscopy in both Marchantia (C74) and Arabidopsis (C75-C77), with BFA treatment confirming TGN/EE localization (C76). The functional complementation data (C78) with quantitative measurements of rosette size and pH provide strong evidence that MpVHA-a is functional at both locations. Western blots confirm expression levels are comparable to controls.

results.result: CRISPR/Cas9-generated vha-a1 null mutants are indistinguishable from wildtype during vegetative growth but are male sterile due to defective pollen development. The pollen defect is rescued by VHA-a1-GFP expression. Genetic crosses show vha-a1 is transmitted through the female but not male gametophyte unless rescued by VHA-a1-GFP. MpVHA-a-mVenus does not rescue the pollen phenotype, indicating the TGN/EE-localized V-ATPase of seed plants has acquired a unique function during pollen development.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C85 present strong genetic evidence from multiple independent CRISPR alleles. The vegetative phenotype (C79), pollen defect (C80), and rescue by VHA-a1-GFP (C81) are clearly documented with Alexander staining. Transmission genetics (C82-C83) properly demonstrate male-specific lethality. The failure of MpVHA-a to rescue (C84) supports the inference of a seed plant-specific function (C85), though the specific function remains unidentified.

results.result: During vegetative growth, VHA-a2 and VHA-a3 compensate for the lack of VHA-a1. vha-a1 mutants are hypersensitive to the V-ATPase inhibitor Concanamycin A, suggesting V-ATPase activity at the TGN/EE. Systematic reduction of VHA-a wildtype alleles through genetic crosses shows that vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+ plants are smaller than vha-a2/+ vha-a3/+, with vha-a1 vha-a2 vha-a3/+ being the smallest viable genotype. The triple homozygous mutant and vha-a1 vha-a2/+ vha-a3 were not recovered, suggesting lethality.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C94 present systematic genetic analysis with quantitative phenotypic measurements. The ConcA hypersensitivity (C86-C88) provides functional evidence for TGN/EE V-ATPase activity in vha-a1. The genetic crosses (C89-C94) are properly controlled and documented, with rosette area measurements showing clear dose-dependent effects of VHA-a allele number. The inference of lethality for certain genotypes (C94) is reasonable given the systematic crossing scheme, though embryo lethality vs. germination failure is not distinguished.

results.result: The authors propose a competition model where VHA-a isoforms compete for entry into COPII vesicles in Arabidopsis cells requiring large amounts of tonoplast membrane. VHA-a1 has higher affinity for Sec24 (COPII cargo receptor) due to the a1-TD, while VHA-a3 (present at ~10-fold higher levels) predominantly enters the Golgi-independent route. In the absence of VHA-a1, VHA-a2/VHA-a3 can enter COPII vesicles more efficiently, compensating for lack of TGN/EE V-ATPase. This explains why RNA knockdown lines show phenotypes while null mutants do not.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C106 present a speculative model that integrates the experimental findings. While the model is logical and consistent with the data (differential ER export, genetic redundancy, expression ratios), it lacks direct evidence for several key assertions: (1) no direct measurement of Sec24 binding affinity (C102), (2) no direct demonstration of competition (C100), (3) the explanation for knockdown vs. null phenotypes (C106) is inferred but not tested. The model is reasonable but requires additional experimental validation.

results.result: The manuscript provides extensive background on V-ATPase structure, function, and differential targeting across eukaryotes. V-ATPases consist of V1 (cytosolic, ATP hydrolysis) and VO (membrane-integral, proton translocation) subcomplexes. Differential targeting is mediated by subunit a isoforms, with targeting information in the N-terminal domain. In Arabidopsis, VHA-a1 targets to TGN/EE while VHA-a2/a3 target to tonoplast. Previous work showed VHA-a1 and VHA-a3 use different ER exit routes (COPII-dependent vs. Golgi-independent).
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C31 represent established knowledge and prior work that is appropriately cited. The citations appear accurate and relevant. This background information provides necessary context for the current study and is well-supported by the literature. The claims about previous findings from the authors' lab (C26-C28, C31) are properly cited to their own publications.

results.result: The authors discuss that differential V-ATPase targeting mediated by subunit a evolved independently in different eukaryotic lineages, with targeting information in different domains (N-terminus in yeast/plants, C-terminus in Paramecium). They speculate that Marchantia might represent an ancestral state with a single VHA-a isoform predominantly at the tonoplast. The identity of VHA-a isoforms can influence biochemical properties including assembly, coupling efficiency, and protein abundance.
results.evaluation: Claims C95 and C97 are supported by appropriate citations to the literature. Claim C96 is explicitly speculative and appropriately qualified as such. The speculation is reasonable given the phylogenetic and functional data presented, though it remains a hypothesis. The discussion appropriately distinguishes between established facts (C95, C97) and speculation (C96).

results.result: The authors infer that VHA-a1 subunits with mutations in the a1-TD that are mislocalized to the tonoplast have retained basal proton-pumping activity and do not require the specific lipid environment of the TGN/EE for functionality, based on their ability to complement the vha-a2 vha-a3 dwarf phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C99 are reasonable inferences from the complementation data (C69-C73). The ability of mislocalized VHA-a1 to partially restore growth and acidify vacuoles demonstrates retained proton-pumping activity. However, the incomplete complementation and failure to reach wildtype pH suggest functional differences that are not fully explained. The inference is appropriately cautious but could benefit from direct biochemical measurements of V-ATPase activity.

results.result: The abstract summarizes the main findings: VHA-a1 targets V-ATPase to TGN/EE while VHA-a2/a3 target to tonoplast; the a1-TD serves as both ER-exit and TGN/EE-retention motif and is conserved in seed plants; Marchantia has a single isoform localizing to both compartments; VHA-a1 is essential for male gametophyte development but redundant with tonoplast isoforms during vegetative growth; the authors propose VHA-a3 is partially rerouted to TGN/EE in the absence of VHA-a1.
results.evaluation: Claims C2-C9 accurately summarize the main findings presented in the manuscript. Claims C2-C8 are well-supported by the experimental data discussed in other result groups. Claim C9 is a proposed model that is reasonable given the genetic redundancy data and ConcA hypersensitivity, though direct visualization of VHA-a3 at the TGN/EE in vha-a1 mutants would strengthen this conclusion.

results.result: The authors cite previous work showing that in the vha-a2 vha-a3 mutant, treatment with V-ATPase inhibitor ConcA causes additional increase in vacuolar pH despite VHA-a1 localization being unaffected, suggesting coordination between TGN/EE and tonoplast V-ATPase activities.
results.evaluation: Claim C105 appropriately cites previous work (Kriegel et al., 2015) and uses it to support the discussion of functional coordination between V-ATPase pools. The citation appears accurate and relevant to the argument being made about the relationship between TGN/EE and tonoplast V-ATPase activities.
